devin: quick heads-up — ran a long-context perf run with quantized KV pages (int8) and hit unexpected memory growth + latency tail after ~25k tokens. attaching short profile: https://ci.internal/runs/176999 — kernel selection looks normal but KV paging/eviction spikes.

maria: ugh. can you paste the alloc/evict trace? was this on Dedicated or local repro?

devin: Dedicated GPU pool, nightly repro. snippet from runtime trace: 
```
KVCache: total_pages=16384 used_slots=12458 free_slots=3926 frag_ratio=0.315
quant_pages(int8)=4320 avg_page_fill=0.47
evictions/sec spike @ 00:23:14 = 128 -> eviction_latency_p99=42ms
resident_mem_before=13.2GB resident_mem_after=15.0GB
```
looks like quantized pages are more fragmented (lower fill) and eviction thrash happens when longctx keeps touching many older segments. batcher holds references for ~1.2s windows causing delayed frees.

sam: interesting — is the fragmentation from smaller key/value pairs after quantization or from page-size mismatch? int8 reduces per-kv size so more slots per page but if the allocator uses same slot size we end up with power-of-two rounding artifacts.

devin: exactly. quantization changed per-slot footprint but we still use the same slot class boundaries -> lots of partially full pages. paging algorithm picks LRU pages but since many slots are in-use across batches they never fully free, causing compaction pressure.

aj: two quick ideas: 1) adapt slot class thresholds when quantized (i.e., recompute expected slot usage per page for int8/bf16) 2) opportunistic compaction during low latency windows (background coalesce). both are low-risk IMO.

maria: +1 on adapting the slot classes. also we should check kernel selection — are we using different kernels for int8 that keep metadata pinned on GPU and block async frees?

devin: good call — profiler shows pinned metadata allocations inside the int8 execution path (nvalloc callstack pointing at fast-matmul int8 kernel). that delays host-side reclamation by ~50-80ms. so there's a two-fold effect: more fragmentation + delayed reclamation.

perf-bot: perf-summary: run=176999, scenario=longctx-100k-tokens, delta_mem=+1.8GB, p99_latency=+18%, evict_rate=+3.2x. flagged tests: kv-eviction-thrash, int8-kernel-pinned-meta.

sam: can we try a quick heuristic: when using quantized model variant (int8), bias alloc to larger slot classes to prefer denser packing? maybe pre-shrink slot header or change page size to 16K -> reduces frag for small entries.

devin: will try two patches in parallel on a repro branch: (A) adaptive slot classes for quantized profiles (B) small-page coalescer + increase compaction aggressiveness after sustained evict spikes. i'll run both with A/B tracing and post results.

maria: add a test that simulates the batching behavior: long sequence of short prompts with overlapping KV touches and a steady batcher window of 1.2s. perf regression historically only shows up with that workload.

aj: also measure quality delta — earlier we've seen INT8 + aggressive compaction sometimes causes tiny regressions around repeat tokens. make sure to pin evaluation harness and diff outputs.

devin: noted — will attach eval diffs. initial expectation: memory drop ~1.1-1.6GB for (A) and lower p99. (B) reduces short-term spikes but may add CPU overhead.

maria: if we land adaptive slots, ensure rollout includes a fallback to previous slot map (config toggle) so Dedicated customers can opt-out if they see unexpected behavior.

devin: yep. planning a canary on 2 low-traffic Dedicated hosts then full rollout. I'll post the branch link + trace summaries when done. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: created issue #INF-1428 kv-quantized-frag for tracking.
